text:
maria: Quick heads-up — trace from the nightly KV-cache perf run has zero line info for a bunch of CUDA kernels when captured with nsys inside the slim container. Perfetto timeline shows kernels labeled as libcuda.so offsets, no function/line demangling. Anyone seen this after switching base images to distroless?

devon: @maria can you paste the exact nsys command + env? Also which CUPTI version are you pulling into the image?

maria: here's the repro command and env (sanitized):
```
NSYS_CMD="nsys profile -o /tmp/run -t cuda,osrt --sample=none --trace-fork=true --force-overwrite --capture-range=cudaApiCalls"
docker run --rm --gpus all -e CUPTI_VERSION=12.1 -v /tmp/run:/out runtime:nightly /bin/sh -c "$NSYS_CMD"
```
Image base: `gcr.io/distroless/base`. Build flags: we compile with `-g` but the packager runs `strip --strip-debug` and we use `-fdebug-prefix-map=$(PWD)=/src` in the build.

sam: are the binaries actually stripped? On CI we sometimes accidentally run `strip` as part of packaging. If build-id/note section is gone, nsys can't map symbols.

maria: confirmed: `readelf -n /app/bin/runtime` in the container shows no NT_GNU_BUILD_ID entry, while host artifact (same build) does have it. But weirdly older traces (before we changed the packager) had lineinfo even when stripped.

devon: two things to check: mismatch between driver and container cupti/libcuda, and whether CUPTI can find the symbol files given path remapping from `-fdebug-prefix-map`. Also check whether `strip` was invoked with `--strip-unneeded` vs `--strip-debug` — the former keeps build-id.

maria: driver on host is 535.86, container ships CUDA toolkit 12.1 (libcudart + libcupti from tarball). I tried setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64` and `CUPTI_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` in the container — no change. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.redwood.dev/trace/abc123 (internal). Kernels appear as `cudaLaunchKernel+0x4a0` with no file/line.

infra-bot: [build-bot] image build 2026-03-17T22:11 finished (sha256:abcd) — includes packaging step: `strip --strip-debug /app/bin/runtime`.

sam: quick local repro I did: run `nsys profile` on the host unstripped binary => line info present. Run same `nsys` inside container with the packaged binary => lineinfo missing. If I run a variant of the image where I skip `strip`, traces regain lineinfo. So strip is likely culprit here.

devon: good catch. That explains immediate symptom. Short term: stop stripping in runtime image. Long term: produce separate dbg tarballs (unstripped), publish symbol server, and teach our nsys/perf CI to use `--symbol-paths`. Also we should add a regression test.

maria: I've pushed a canary image `ci-canary:keep-debug` (sha256:cand) that omits the strip step. I re-ran nsys inside that container and lineinfo returned. I'll open a PR to remove strip and keep a debug artifacts workflow.

sam: let's also add a small CI trace assertion: run a tiny kernel with nsys inside container and assert at least 80% of CUDA samples have `source` present in nsys report. That would catch this early.

devon: also let's add a note in ops runbook: when tracing inside distroless, ensure build-id is preserved or provide symbols via `--symbol-paths`. And watch CUPTI/nsys compatibility: nsys version sometimes expects a matching CUPTI (pkg mismatch causes weird mapping failures).

maria: FYI I opened an issue with reproducer + traces + container diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2345 — includes steps to reproduce locally.

ops-greg: noted, removing strip could bump image size. Ops will schedule a short deploy window to roll this change and monitor disk usage. tagging @ops.

maria: action items: 1) PR to stop strip in packager (WIP), 2) create dbg tarball artifact + symbol publish, 3) add CI nsys smoke test, 4) update ops runbook. I'll follow up in the issue.

devon: thanks @maria. Also add a brief note in the Dedicated rollout doc since we use the same packager for dedicated images.

maria: will do. thanks all :pray:

sam: TL;DR — missing lineinfo was caused by strip removing build-id / debug sections in packaged image; proof: unstripped canary image restores lines. Next steps above.
